title: Angular CDK Deep Dive: Virtual Scroll & Drag/Drop

options.text: Renders every list item but hides the off-screen ones with CSS
Renders only the DOM elements currently visible (plus a small buffer), recycling nodes as you scroll
Loads the whole list from the server at once

questions.explanation: Only the visible window of items is in the DOM, so a 100,000-row list scrolls like a 20-row one.

questions.prompt: Why must a cdk-virtual-scroll-viewport have an explicit height in CSS?

options.text: The CDK computes the visible item range from the viewport's dimensions and scroll offset; without a bounded height there's nothing to scroll

questions.explanation: A bounded height (plus itemSize) lets the FixedSizeVirtualScrollStrategy calculate which rows to render.

questions.prompt: After a drag, who is responsible for updating your underlying data array?

options.text: The CDK updates the data automatically
You are — in the (cdkDropListDropped) handler, using moveItemInArray or transferArrayItem

questions.explanation: The CDK only moves the visual representation; you own the data and call the helper functions in the drop handler.

questions.prompt: Match each drag/drop helper or directive to its role.

pairs.right: Move an item between two lists' arrays
Restrict the grabbable area to a child element

questions.explanation: These building blocks compose into reorderable and Kanban-style interfaces.

questions.prompt: You use moveItemInArray on a signal-backed array under OnPush, but the UI doesn't update. Why?

options.text: The helper mutates the array in place, so you must replace the reference (e.g. signal.update(a => [...a]))

questions.explanation: moveItemInArray/transferArrayItem mutate by reference; produce a new reference or call markForCheck() so change detection picks it up.

questions.prompt: For fixed-size virtual scrolling, which viewport attribute must match the real pixel height of one row?
questions.explanation: A mismatched itemSize is the #1 cause of janky/jumpy virtual scrolling.
